html:
The Arikara, or Sahnish, are a Native American people of the upper Missouri River in the Dakotas. They speak a Caddoan language close to that of the Pawnee, from whom they split long ago.

They lived in fortified villages of earth lodges and grew maize, beans and squash. Their villages were trading centres where Plains nomads swapped meat and hides for corn, and later horses and guns.

Smallpox struck them hard in the 1780s and again in 1837, and raids by the Lakota pushed them north. They met the Lewis and Clark Expedition in 1804 and fought the US Army in 1823. In the 1860s they joined the Mandan and Hidatsa at Like-a-Fishhook village. Today they are part of the Mandan, Hidatsa and Arikara Nation at Fort Berthold.
